subject: Proposal: annual prepay on-ramp with performance holdback and term credits
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@nimblehealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Finance Ops <finance@nimblehealth.com>
Date: 2026-04-26T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring a move from monthly to annual prepay (pricing questions)

Hi Mateo —

Weve been running Redwood on monthly billing during our pilot and are planning to centralize vendor billing for FY27. Finance is pushing us toward an annual prepay. Before we take that to procurement I want to surface a few questions so I can build a recommendation: 

- What term discounts do you offer for a 12-month prepay vs our current monthly spend? Any additional uplift for a 24-month commitment?
- We expect consumption to step up over the first 3 quarters. Do you offer ramp credits or usage holdback mechanisms if usage exceeds our prepay early on?
- What protections are there if service performance or latency degrades during ramp?

Short background: current monthly run-rate ~ $35k USD; projected Yr1 usage distribution is 40% Q1, 60% Q2, 100% Q3 onward (we estimate). Were mainly concerned about overcommitting and having liquidity tied up while usage ramps.

Can you send an initial structure we can review with finance?

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Product
NimbleHealth

Attachment: none

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-27T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring a move from monthly to annual prepay (pricing questions)

Alex —

Thanks for the context and the consumption curve. High level response up front: yes, we can do an annual prepay with a tiered term discount and a structured "on-ramp" that minimizes your downside while unlocking material pricing improvement versus monthly billing.

Key points below; I attached a spreadsheet with an example cadence (Nimble_Onramp_Term_Schedule_v1.xlsx) and a draft ordering document.

1) Term discounts
- 12-month prepay: 15% discount on our standard usage rates relative to pay-as-you-go.
- 24-month prepay: 20% discount + price protection for year 2 (no upward indexation beyond CPI cap).

2) Ramp / usage holdback concept (to address liquidity concerns)
- We propose a 3-quarter phased on-ramp where 60% of the committed FY spend is invoiced upfront, and 40% is treated as a usage holdback that can be reclaimed as credits tied to actual consumption.
- If usage in Q1+Q2 is below ramp targets, we credit unused holdback back to you as account credit or offset against future invoices.

3) Performance guardrail / SLA path
- We include a 30-day operational review window during the first 90 days post-signed order. If latency or error rates breach agreed SLOs, we will deploy a priority escalation path (dedicated SRE on-call) and issue proportional service credits if we miss remediation milestones.

4) Reconciliation and true-up
- Quarterly true-up to align committed vs actual consumption; any over-usage is billed at a reduced overage rate (our prepay rate + 5%).

Next steps I propose:
- If this structure looks acceptable, Marissa will draft a firm order form and Ben will validate the finance terms for your AP team.
- Can you confirm Nimbles preferred billing (PO vs credit card) and billing contact so we can include payment terms in the SaaS order?

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Nimble_Onramp_Term_Schedule_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet: proposed billing cadence & credit math)
- Draft_SaaS_Order_NimbleHealth.pdf (stubbed order form)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@nimblehealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Finance Ops <finance@nimblehealth.com>
Date: 2026-04-29T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring a move from monthly to annual prepay (pricing questions)

Mateo —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the spreadsheet. A few clarifying requests from procurement/finance after reviewing the files: 

- The 60/40 invoice/holdback split seems reasonable, but finance wants an explicit mechanism for early-release of holdback credits if we exceed the committed usage during Q1/Q2 (so we don't sit on a credit while our usage spikes). Can you make the early-release automatic when cumulative usage >= committed percent thresholds?
- We need clearer definitions on the operational SLOs that trigger the remediation path and the size of proportional service credits. Finance wants a deterministic credit formula for budgeting.
- Can Redwood offer a one-time onboarding credit (applied to Q1) if we sign a 24-month prepay? Even a modest concession here would help our internal ROI calc.

Also for procurement: preferred payment via PO with Net30. Who should we route the PO to on your side?

If you can update the term schedule to call these items out explicitly, we can move to redlines next week.

Best,
Alex

Alex —

Appreciate the constructive feedback. Quick answers and an updated path forward below. Ben and I will incorporate the edits into an updated order form and send for your review tomorrow.

Actionable updates we will put in the revised term schedule: 
- Early-release holdback: automatic release triggers when cumulative billed usage reaches 80% of the committed amount for the applicable period. That release will offset your outstanding invoices or be applied as a credit per your preference.
- SLA credit formula: we will add a deterministic table (latency tiers x credit %) and a remediation timeline (T+48hrs to acknowledge, T+7 days remediation plan, escalated SRE if unresolved). The spreadsheet will include illustrative numbers so your finance team can model it.
- 24-month sign-on credit: we can add a one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of Year 1 committed spend, applied in Q1 invoice, conditional on signature and PO within 30 days.
- PO routing: please send the PO to finance-ops@redwood.com and reference DEAL-2026-0397. Our AP team supports Net30.

Next steps:
- Ben will update the pricing appendix to show final effective blended rates across ramp quarters.
- We will send a DocuSign-ready order form and a clean term schedule tomorrow for redlines.

If that aligns, ping me and we will prioritize the document so procurement can start their review.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
